extracted.intended_audience: library patrons, legal researchers, and members of the public seeking Texas administrative rules or guidance on where to find them
extracted.subtask_description: A practical guide to where Texas administrative rules are published, how rulemaking is governed, and how to locate historical and current agency rules (Texas Administrative Code and Texas Register). Useful for people doing legal research or looking up agency rules and rulemaking notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency rulemaking authority (enabling statutes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas Legislature creates agencies and commissions to help administer the law. The statutes that create the agencies describe their responsibilities and often give them rulemaking powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The Department of Public Safety (DPS) is responsible for administering driver licenses; these responsibilities are outlined in Chapter 521 of the Transportation Code, and DPS creates rules addressing specific details (e.g., acceptable identification). In short, an agency can only make rules to the extent its enabling statute grants rulemaking authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking process governed by Chapter 2001, Government Code (Administrative Procedure Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rulemaking process is set out in Chapter 2001 of the Government Code. This chapter is known as the Administrative Procedure Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 2001 contains the procedural requirements agencies must follow when proposing, adopting, withdrawing, or issuing emergency rules. Researchers should consult the APA when evaluating whether rulemaking steps were followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Texas Administrative Code (TAC) is the official compiled rules, organized by subject and updated annually
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency rules are compiled and organized by subject matter by the Texas Secretary of State as the Texas Administrative Code. It is updated annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The library holds print copies of the Texas Administrative Code dating back to 1979; if you cannot visit in person, use Ask a Librarian for assistance. Use the TAC to find current agency rules organized by subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Texas Register publishes all rulemaking actions and related notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the Administrative Code are published in the Texas Register, which serves as the journal of state agency rulemaking in Texas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Texas Register publishes proposed, adopted, withdrawn and emergency rule actions; notices of state agency review of agency rules; governor's appointments; attorney general opinions; and miscellaneous documents such as requests for proposals. Previous issues are available on the secretary of state's website and online at the Portal to Texas History.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical rules access limits and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical access to administrative rules varies by format and date: the online version allows searching rules as they existed on particular dates going back to January 1, 1999; the library has print TAC copies from 1979 onward; for rules created before 1979, you must contact the agency directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If agency records pre-1979 were transferred, they may be at the Texas State Library and Archives — contact their reference desk. For help locating older editions or historical rules, Ask a Librarian by phone or e-mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library assistance limitation / disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: The library cannot tell you what the law means for your situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The library can help you locate rule texts, registers, and historical materials and provides services (Ask a Librarian, print copies, reference desk), but it does not provide legal interpretation or advice.
